requirements.requirement: The system must define a sponsor_credibility schema object compatible with existing clinical trial Pydantic models.
The system must include a sponsor_type field with allowed values: NIH, academic, pharmaceutical, other.
The system must enforce sponsor_type as a required field in the schema.
The system must include a historical_credibility_score field constrained to a numeric range between 0 and 1 inclusive.
The system must include a final_normalized_score field constrained to a numeric range between 0 and 1 inclusive.
The system must define an internal scoring contract specifying input fields and output structure for sponsor credibility.
The system must ensure the scoring contract output structure matches the format expected by downstream evaluation pipeline components.
The system must validate that all numeric fields in the schema reject values outside the 0 to 1 range.
The system must support serialization and deserialization of the sponsor credibility schema without data loss.
The system must gracefully handle missing sponsor_type input by defaulting to 'other' in the schema.
The system must set historical_credibility_score to a default value of 0.5 when no historical data is available.
The system must ensure schema compatibility with existing clinical_trials_models.py without requiring breaking changes.
The system must enable LLM components to consume the schema and interpret sponsor_type consistently across all allowed values.
The system must ensure LLM outputs referencing sponsor credibility adhere strictly to the defined schema fields and value ranges.
The system must prevent LLM-generated values from introducing undefined sponsor_type categories outside the allowed set.
The system must ensure LLM components map ambiguous sponsor descriptions to one of the allowed sponsor_type values or 'other'.
The system must validate that any LLM-produced historical_credibility_score is numeric and within the 0 to 1 range before acceptance.
The system must ensure LLM-generated schema instances can be programmatically validated using the same Pydantic model as non-LLM inputs.
